facts.statement: Fossils of Hollanda were found at Khermeen Tsav and date to about 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Found at Khermeen Tsav, it dates from the late Cretaceous period (Campanian stage), about 75 million years ago.

facts.statement: Hollanda is known only from partial hind limbs that feature long legs and an unusual toe configuration.
facts.quote: Known only from partial hind limbs, Hollanda has long legs with an unusual configuration of the toes.

facts.statement: Hollanda is classified within the parent group Ornithuromorpha.
Hollanda is classified under the class Reptilia.
The time range for Hollanda is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species was named by Alyssa Bell after the Holland family, who donated to the project, and the rock band Lucero.
facts.quote: Alyssa Bell, named the new species after the Holland family (donors to the project) and the rock band Lucero.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding Hollanda's classification, with studies placing it in the Ornithurae, the primitive family Songlingornithidae, the family Gansuidae, or as an enantiornithean.
facts.quote: Some studies have found that it was a relatively advanced bird, a member of the Ornithurae, related to birds like Ichthyornis. Other studies have recovered it as a member of the primitive family Songlingornithidae or derived member of the family Gansuidae. A more expansive study found it as an enantiornithean.

rejected.statement: Hollanda is a genus of small ground birds known from fossils found in the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia.
